fill: findings: one per material observation the document makes about a verse (CP-01 to CP-07); lines[].answer: every line answered (captured / already_recorded / not_an_observation)

lines.text: | AN-01 | Anger is very often kindled by **something perceived**: heard or seen, stated in the verse itself | Gen 34:7; 39:19; Exo 32:19; 1Sa 11:6; 17:28; 2Sa 13:21; Neh 4:1; 5:6; Est 3:5; 5:9; Job 32:5; Psa 112:10; Mat 2:16; 20:24; 21:15; Luk 4:28; Act 7:54; 17:16 | S (count limited to the texts cited) | 10.1, 10.2, 10.0 | W (10.2 → 10.1: hearing feeds feeling) |
| AN-02 | It can be kindled by **a lie**, and act on it anyway | Gen 39:19 (Potiphar); Jer 37:13–15 | S | 10.1, 10.9 | W |
| AN-03 | The angry one **misreads the other's heart** | 1Sa 17:28 ("I know … the evil of your heart"); Gen 30:1–2 | S | 10.3, 10.9 | W (anger reckons wrongly, like 10.3) |

| AN-04 | Anger comes **where a lifted state is checked**: the heart lifted by strength (Uzziah), the merry heart (Ahasuerus), the glad heart (Haman), the heart already set (Dan 11:28) | 2Ch 26:16, 19; Est 1:10–12; 5:9; Dan 11:28–30 | S (sequence) / R (link) | 11 §2, 10.1 | W (11 §2: the threshold pattern, now with anger) |

| AN-05 | **Four occasions of blocked will:** a demand no one can meet; being thwarted or made a fool of; rebuke from a holy person; refusal by an inferior | Gen 30:2; Dan 2:12 · Num 22:29; 2Ki 5:11; Mat 2:16 · 2Ch 16:10; 26:19 · Est 1:12; Dan 3:19 | S | 10.1, 10.6 | W |

| AN-06 | **A rival's rise:** the anger reckons the rival's future ("what more can he have but the kingdom?"), watches ("eyed"), and enlarges its target | 1Sa 18:8–9; 20:30; Neh 4:1; Est 3:5–6; Psa 112:10; Mat 20:24 | S | 10.3, 10.9, 11 §6 | W (anger becomes reckoning and plot: 1Sa 18:8 → 18:25) |

| AN-07 | **Indignation for another** who is wronged; it states a norm ("such a thing must not be done") | Gen 34:7; 1Sa 20:34; 2Sa 12:5; Neh 5:6; Psa 119:53; Act 17:16; Mar 10:14 | S | 10.7, 10.9 | W |

| AN-08 | **Anger at what God has done**, at his striking (Uzzah) and at his **mercy** (Jonah, who quotes "slow to anger" against him) | 2Sa 6:8; Num 11:10; 1Sa 15:11; Jon 4:1–2; Pro 19:3 ("his heart rages against the Lord", misdirected) | S | 10.8 | W |
| AN-09 | **Indignation at good done**, defending a norm against it | Mat 21:15; 26:8; Mar 14:4; Luk 13:14; Joh 7:23; Act 4:2 | S | 10.7, 10.9 | W |

| AN-10 | **Rage at the word** that lowers the hearers' standing or exposes their guilt. It stops its ears | Luk 4:28; Act 5:33; 7:54, 57; 19:28 | S | 10.2, 10.4 | W (10.2: refusing to hear, now with rage) |
| AN-11 | **The fallen face:** anger that cannot reach its cause sinks into the body (face, bed, no food), and comes out as a death | Gen 4:5–8; 1Ki 21:4–16 | S | 10.1, Ch 6, 14 | W |

| AN-12 | **Someone else names it.** God asks Cain; Jezebel names Ahab's spirit; Elkanah names Hannah's heart. The two offers that follow are opposites: "rule over it" or "I will give you the vineyard" | Gen 4:6–7; 1Ki 21:5–7; 1Sa 1:8 | S | 10.9, 14 | W |
| AN-13 | **Anger is kept going by a plan that soothes it** ("comforts himself … by planning to kill you") | Gen 27:41–42 | S | 10.3, 10.0 | W (the path: anger → inner sentence → plan) |

| AN-14 | **Anger has a course in time:** it turns away and is forgotten (Esau); is kept "forever" (Edom); repeats (Pro 19:19); is to end before sunset (Eph 4:26–27) | Gen 27:44–45; 33:4; Amo 1:11; Pro 19:19; Eph 4:26–27 | S | 10.1, 11 §4, NS-M3 | W; feeds NS-M3 (remembering and forgetting) |
| AN-15 | **Anger lodges and is cherished**, and the lodging is the fool's | Ecc 7:9; Job 36:13 | S | Ch 7, 10.1 | W (Ch 7 already has Ecc 7:9; add Job 36:13) |

| AN-16 | **Held anger released as a ledger** ("these twenty years"; "these many years"); pressure in the belly, and speech as relief | Gen 31:36–39; 2Sa 3:8; Job 32:2–20; Luk 15:28–29 | S | 10.4, 10.1 | W |
| AN-17 | **Anger turned on oneself**: wounding the self; forbidden by Joseph | Job 18:4; Gen 45:5; Jon 4:3, 8–9 | S | 10.1, 12 | W |

| AN-18 | **Fretting = heating oneself** at the wicked's success. It "tends only to evil". It is replaced by trust, committing, stillness and waiting | Psa 37:1–9; Pro 24:19 | S | 10.1, 10.8, 13 | W |

| AN-19 | **Vexation suffered**: worn down year by year, in the eye and the body, sleepless; met by being heard; Qoheleth's vexation of knowing and working; "sorrow is better than laughter" | 1Sa 1:6–18; Job 6:2; 17:7; Psa 6:7–9; 10:14; 31:9; Ecc 1:18; 2:23; 7:3; 11:10 | S | 10.1, Ch 6 | W |

| AN-20 | **Anger and grief, joined.** Jonathan's grief is for David (1Sa 20:34). Jesus "looked around at them with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart" (Mar 3:5): one object for both | 1Sa 20:34; Mar 3:5 | S | 10.1, 10.8 | W |
| AN-21 | **Fear and anger follow one another**: anger at God, then fear of God (2Sa 6:8–9); fear first, then anger at a weaker target (Dan 11:30) | 2Sa 6:8–9; Dan 11:30, 44 | S | 10.1 | W |
| AN-22 | **Kinship stops strife or feeds it**, on the same ground ("for we are kinsmen" / "the king is our close relative") | Gen 13:8–9; 2Sa 19:42–43; Pro 18:19 | S | 10.9, 11 §4 | W |
| AN-23 | **Anger at a brother is judged like murder; worship waits on reconciliation** | Mat 5:22–24 | S | 10.9, 10.8 | W |

| AN-24 | **The powerful one's anger** decides others' fate; those beneath plead, read it, script a reply, reach it through an intermediary | Gen 40:2–3; 44:18; 1Sa 20:7; 2Sa 11:20–21; Est 7:7; Pro 19:12; 20:2; Act 12:20 | S | 10.9 | W |
| AN-25 | **The oppressor's wrath is shown with its end in view**: the strength that carries it breaks | Isa 14:4–7; Pro 22:8; Dan 8:6–8 | S | 10.9, 11 | W |
| AN-26 | **The leader's anger** at those he leads: it flares, breaks, questions, and **yields to a reason** | Exo 32:19–20; Lev 10:16–20; Num 16:15; 2Ki 13:19 | S | 10.9 | W |
| AN-27 | **Anger is learned from company**, and the self is what is snared | Pro 22:24–25; Gen 49:6–7 | S | 10.9, 11 §6 | W (11 §6: inner states pass between people) |

| AN-28 | **How strife is kindled and quenched**: fuel, pressure ("pressing anger produces strife"), a whisperer, wine, the lot | Pro 15:18; 26:20–21; 30:33; 29:22; 23:29–30; 18:18 | S | 10.9, 10.4 | W |
| AN-29 | **Turning another's anger away**: a soft answer, patience, a soft tongue, a gift (reported, not approved) | Pro 15:1; 16:14; 25:15; 21:14; 29:8; 2Ki 5:13 | S | 10.4, 10.9 | W |
| AN-30 | **The quarrelsome house**: dripping, not a storm; the one who bears it withdraws | Pro 19:13; 21:9, 19; 25:24; 27:15–16 | S | 10.9 | W |

| AN-31 | **Strife among believers is traced to an inner source**: passions at war within, the flesh, conceit, appetite, envy behind preaching | Jam 4:1–3; 1Co 3:3; Gal 5:26; 1Ti 6:4–5; Phili 1:15–17; Rom 16:18 | S | 10.9, 10.5, 12 | W |

| AN-32 | **Anger in the lists**: its constant neighbours are envy, jealousy and speech-sins. It is set straight after "do not grieve the Holy Spirit" | Gal 5:19–21; Eph 4:30–32; Col 3:8; 2Co 12:20; Rom 1:29; 13:13 | S | 12, 13 | W |

| AN-33 | **The enemy's anger as the one attacked bears it**: swallowing, grudge, venom in speech; felt as "my heart is in anguish within me" (Psa 55:4); answered by calling on God | Psa 55:3–5; 124:3; 140:3; 58:4; 7:6; 2Co 7:5 ("fighting without and fear within") | S | 10.1, 10.8, 10.9 | W |
| AN-34 | **Fear of another's anger, and freedom from it**: forgetting God feeds it; seeing the invisible frees from it | Isa 7:2–9; 51:12–13; Heb 11:27; Dan 1:8–12 | S | 10.1, 10.8 | W |
| AN-35 | **Anger poured as a drink** to shame another, and the cup comes back | Hab 2:15–16; Rev 14:8–10 | S | 10.0 (what comes back), 10.9 | W |

| AN-36 | **"Long of nostrils"**: slow to anger is understanding, glory, better than the mighty; ruling one's spirit is better than taking a city | Pro 14:29; 16:32; 19:11; Jam 1:19 | S | 11 §7, Ch 5 | W (Ch 5 and 11 §7 already carry Pro 14:29 and 16:32) |
| AN-37 | **Human anger does not produce God's righteousness**; slowness opens the way to receiving the word | Jam 1:19–21 | S | 10.2, 13 | W |
| AN-38 | **"Be angry and do not sin"**: anger itself is not forbidden; leaving it overnight opens a door to the devil | Eph 4:26–27 | S | 10.1, 12 | W |
| AN-39 | **Love is not irritable**: it does not get provoked | 1Co 13:5 | S | 10.9 | W |

| AN-40 | **Human anger related to God's in four ways:** given with the Spirit (Saul, ending in mercy that day); shared as God's jealousy (Phinehas, "counted to him as righteousness"); exceeding the commission ("a rage that has reached up to heaven"); **used** ("the wrath of man shall praise you") | 1Sa 11:6, 13; Num 25:11; Psa 106:30–31; 2Ch 28:9–15; Psa 76:10 | S | 10.8, 11 §4 | W |

| AN-41 | **The prophet as vessel**: God's anger in a human comes out as suffering, not violence: weariness, isolation, bitterness, seven days overwhelmed | Jer 6:10–11; 15:16–18; Eze 3:14–15; Jer 8:18, 21 | S | 10.8, 10.1 | W |

| AN-42 | **Who may pronounce anger**: a curse cannot go beyond God's ("How can I curse whom God has not cursed?"); the same verb is valid when it follows justice | Num 23:8; Pro 24:24; Job 40:9–14 | S | 10.4, 10.7 | W |
| AN-43 | **Jesus's anger**: it looks, grieves and heals. Their silence becomes a plot | Mar 3:4–6; 10:14–16 | S | 10.1, 10.8, 11 §4 | W |
| AN-44 | **Provoking and indignation turned to good**: stirring one another to love; indignation as the fruit of godly grief | Heb 10:24; 2Co 7:10–11; 9:2 | S | 11 §4, 13 | W |

| AN-45 | **The answer to human anger is most often a question or a reframing, not a rebuke**: God's question to Cain and to Jonah; Joseph's "not you … but God"; the father's "this your brother"; Jesus redefining greatness and the norm; Nathan's parable | Gen 4:6; Jon 4:4, 9–11; Gen 45:5–8; Luk 15:31–32; Mat 20:25–26; Luk 13:15–16; 2Sa 12:7 | S (instances) / R (pattern) | 10.9, 10.8, 11 | W |
| AN-46 | **Twice the text ends before the angry one answers** (Jonah; the elder brother) | Jon 4:11; Luk 15:32 | S | 11 | W (left open in the narrative too) |

| AN-47 | **Answered by turning to God instead**: be still and wait; ponder on your bed and be silent; leave it to the wrath of God and feed the enemy | Psa 37:7–8; Psa 4:4; Rom 12:19–21 | S | 10.8, 10.9, 13 | W |

| AN-48 | **Human anger is often shown with no inner word at all.** It is carried by the act, the face and body, speech, another person naming it, "to themselves", a word that holds the seat inside it (*aph* = nostril), or the frame of a list | pilot §3; Gen 4:5; Mar 14:4; Gal 5:19 | S / R | Ch 14 | RS (Ch 14 "Beyond the named words" gains this) |

| AN-49 | **Narrative shows anger by its act; wisdom places it in the heart or spirit**, where it can be governed or judged | U1 §38 point 1: Job 36:13; Pro 14:29; 16:32; 19:3; Ecc 7:9 against the narratives | R | Ch 14, 11 | W (as a reading) |

| AN-50 | **The inner word is often named in the other party, or in the contrast figure**: the opponents' hardened heart (Mar 3:5); the builders' "mind to work" (Neh 4:6); "his heart is steady" (Psa 112:8); Daniel "resolved" (Dan 1:8); Stephen "full of the Holy Spirit" (Act 7:55) | as listed | S / R | Ch 14, 11 | W |

| AN-51 | **Provoking God, and its named inner roots**: forgetting; fullness ("grew fat, and kicked"); a deceived or turning heart; false security ("I shall be safe, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart"); distress that drives further away (Ahaz); not believing; never satisfied | Deu 32:15, 18; 31:20; 11:16; 29:19; 1Ki 11:4, 9; 2Ch 28:22; 2Ki 17:14; Eze 16:28 | S | 12, NS-M2 | NS-M2 / W (12) |

| AN-52 | **The provocation turns on the provoker**: "Is it I whom they provoke? … Is it not themselves, to their own shame?"; they "became false" | Jer 7:19; 25:7; 2Ki 17:15 | S | 10.0 (what comes back), 12 | W |

| AN-53 | **Provocation handed on**: "made Israel to sin"; "like mother, like daughter"; the leader's failure leaves the people without a shepherd | 1Ki 14:16; 16:2, 33; Eze 16:44; Zec 10:2–3 | S | 11 §6, 12 | W |
| AN-54 | **Asking once more, aware of the anger**: boldness and restraint in one sentence; the anger feared never comes | Gen 18:30–32; Judg 6:39 | S | 10.8 | W |

| AN-55 | **Intercession: standing in the breach**; driven by the intercessor's own fear; answered (Moses), forbidden (Jer 7:16), sought and not found (Eze 22:30), refused (Eze 9:8), insufficient (Eze 14:20), turned to imprecation (Jer 18:20–23); and the one explained by God's anger prays for the explainers (Job 42:8) | Exo 32:10–14; Deu 9:18–20; Psa 106:23; Jer 7:16; Eze 22:30; 9:8–10; 14:20; Jer 18:20–23; Job 42:8–10 | S | 10.8, 10.9, NS-M2 | NS-M2 |

| AN-56 | **"Slow to anger" received and used eight ways**: worship, plea, confession, complaint (Jonah), praise, wonder, judgement (Nahum), ground for returning (Joel). **One creed; its character changes with the one who uses it** | Exo 34:6–8; Num 14:18–19; Neh 9:17; Jon 4:2; Psa 145:8; Mic 7:18; Nah 1:3; Joe 2:13 | S | 10.8, 11 §4 | W (11 §4 change of character) |

| AN-57 | **The heart that turns, and so turns the anger**: Josiah's tender heart; Rehoboam; Hezekiah humbled "for the pride of his heart"; partial humbling (Rehoboam "did not set his heart") | 2Ki 22:19; 2Ch 12:6–7, 12, 14; 32:25–26; 1Ki 8:47–48 | S | 13, NS-M2 | NS-M2 / W (13) |

| AN-58 | **The heart that does not take the blow in**, and the heart made "diamond-hard lest they should hear" | Isa 42:25; 9:13; Jer 12:11; Zec 7:11–13; Mal 1:4; Rom 2:5 | S | 12 | W (12 hardening; Rom 2:5 is already there) |

| AN-59 | **Distress goes both ways**: it brings the cry (Judges; Manasseh), more faithlessness (Ahaz), or flight into the wrath (the remnant in Egypt). The texts do not say why | Judg 2:18; 2Ch 33:12; 28:22; Jer 42:16; 44:10 | S | 11 §4 | W (change of character: distress) |
| AN-60 | **God answers the cry and the groaning, not a completed repentance** | Judg 2:18; 10:16; Psa 106:43–45 | S | 10.8 | W |

| AN-61 | **Reading the ruin**: "Why?"; reading it rightly is the first step back; reading it as God's absence; seeing it and not turning; understood only afterwards ("In the latter days you will understand") | Deu 29:24–29; 31:17; 2Ch 29:8; Jer 8:19; 44:2; 23:20; Eze 36:20 | S | 10.2, 10.3, NS-M2 | NS-M2 |
| AN-62 | **Knowledge through the anger**: "they shall know that I am the Lord"; for knowledge of his rule, his purpose, his name | Eze 5:13; 7:9; 25:17; Psa 59:13 | S | 10.2, NS-M2 | NS-M2 |
| AN-63 | **Asking for the measure**: "Correct me, O Lord, but in justice; not in your anger"; the bearer names his own sin or limits | Psa 6:1–3; 38:1–5; Jer 10:23–24 | S | 10.8 | W |
| AN-64 | **Fear of being cast off, answered by remembering** | Psa 27:8–10; 77:7–11 | S | 10.8, NS-M3 | W; feeds NS-M3 |

| AN-65 | **"For a moment"**: the anger that passes, measured by what follows it ("joy comes with the morning"); "I will not be angry with you" | Psa 30:5–7; Isa 54:7–9; 12:1; Jer 32:37–39 | S | 10.8, 13 | W |

| AN-66 | **Community lament**: why? how long? restore us. The anger is felt as reaching even prayer, and as taking away the will to pray | Psa 74:1; 79:5; 80:4; 85:4–6; 89:46; Isa 64:5–9 | S | 10.8, NS-M2 | NS-M2 |

| AN-67 | **Zion's lament from inside**: body, hunger, the heart poured out, hope in the middle ("he does not afflict from his heart"), and an unfinished question at the end | Lam 1:12–13; 2:19; 3:1–33, 40–44; 5:21–22 | S | 10.1, 10.8, NS-M2 | NS-M2 |
| AN-68 | **Bearing God's anger without knowing why** (Job; Psalm 88, which has no turn) | Job 6:4; 9:13–16; 14:13–15; 16:9; 19:11; Psa 88:7–18; 102:9–10 | S | 10.1, 10.8, NS-M2 | NS-M2 |
| AN-69 | **Bearing it willingly because of one's sin**, expecting the same God to plead one's cause | Mic 7:7–10; Lam 3:39 | S | 10.8, 13 | W |
| AN-70 | **Mortal life lived under the wrath; considering it is the way to a heart of wisdom** | Psa 90:7–12 | S | Ch 9, 10.3 | W |
| AN-71 | **Who can stand?**: awe, and refuge in the same God | Psa 76:7–9; Nah 1:6–7; Psa 2:12; Rev 6:17 | S | 10.8 | W |

| AN-72 | **Shelter while it passes**: God tells his people to hide (Isa 26:20), as Job asked (Job 14:13). The reverse is to ask the mountains to hide one *from* God (Rev 6:16) | Isa 26:20; Job 14:13; Zep 2:3; Rev 6:16 | S | 10.8, NS-M2 | NS-M2 |

| AN-73 | **False peace**: "surely his anger has turned from me"; "It shall be well with you"; "We have Abraham as our father"; "Let no one deceive you with empty words" | Jer 2:35; 23:17; Deu 29:19; Mat 3:9; Eph 5:6 | S | 12 | W |
| AN-74 | **"Who knows?"**: returning without a guarantee | Joe 2:12–14; Jon 3:9–10; Zep 2:3; Jer 36:7 | S | 13, 10.6 | W |
| AN-75 | **God gives the words to return with**, and the anger turns | Hos 14:2–4; Jer 3:12–13 | S | 13, 10.4 | W |

| AN-76 | **"Rend your hearts and not your garments"**: outward signs are not refused, but the heart is what must be torn; circumcise the heart; "did not return to me with her whole heart, but in pretense" | Joe 2:13; Jer 4:4; 3:10 | S | 13, 10.6 | W |

| AN-77 | **The agent of wrath with a heart of its own** goes beyond the measure and is judged; the appointed agent; the agent who did not carry it out | Isa 10:5–12; 47:6–8; Zec 1:15; Rom 13:4–5; 1Sa 28:18 | S | 10.6, 11 §1 | W (11 §1: acted upon, yet with its own purpose; Isa 10:7 is already in 10.6) |
| AN-78 | **One sins, all bear**; the one who sinned asks to bear it alone | Jos 7:1; 22:18–20; 2Sa 24:17 | S | 10.9, 11 §6 | W |

| AN-79 | **Near the holy**: the priest's grief withheld lest wrath come; David's anger, then fear, then **resolved by watching another household live with the ark** | Lev 10:3, 6; 2Sa 6:8–12 | S | 10.8, 10.1 | W |
| AN-80 | **Mourning commanded** because the wrath has come; mourning forbidden lest it come | Jer 4:8; 7:29; Lev 10:6 | S | 10.1, 11 §4 | W (change of character: mourning) |

| AN-81 | **What the people asked for is answered in anger**: a king given in anger; craving granted; "Let us be like the nations" refused | Hos 13:11; Psa 78:29–31; Eze 20:32–33 | S | 10.5, 12 | W (wanting) |

| AN-82 | **Restraint, and the reasons God gives**: they are flesh; the spirit would faint; for my name's sake; "I am God and not a man". Two of the reasons are about what the human is | Psa 78:38–39; Isa 57:16; 48:9; Hos 11:8–9 | S | Ch 9, 11 §8 | W |
| AN-83 | **Kindness meant to lead to repentance; wrath stored up by a hard heart** | Rom 2:4–5 | S | 12, 13 | W (Rom 2:5 is in 12) |
| AN-84 | **Delivered from the wrath to come**: the response is waiting, soberness and encouraging one another, not fear | Rom 5:8–10; Eph 2:3–5; 1Th 1:9–10; 5:8–11 | S | 13 | W |
| AN-85 | **Vengeance renounced and left to God's wrath**; the enemy fed | Rom 12:17–21 | S | 10.9, 13 | W |
| AN-86 | **Put off what the wrath comes on**, including one's own anger (Col 3:6 then 3:8) | Col 3:5–10; Eph 5:6–8 | S | 13 | W |
| AN-87 | **Those who come through sing that it is just**; those struck curse and do not repent | Rev 15:2–3; 16:9, 11, 21 | S | 10.8, 13 | W |

| AN-88 | **The clay pleads with the potter (Isaiah); the clay is told not to answer back (Romans)** | Isa 64:8–9; Rom 9:20–22 | S | 10.8, 11 §1 | W (11 §1: the potter image already there via *yēṣer*) |
| AN-89 | **Injustice draws the wrath as surely as idols do**; God's anger is for the widow, the orphan and the debtor who cry | Exo 22:22–27; Hos 5:10; Mic 6:8–12; Jer 21:12 | S | 10.7, 10.9 | W |

| AN-90 | **The wilderness provocation is to be remembered**, as a cure for the heart's claim to righteousness ("Do not say in your heart … 'because of my righteousness'"), and made a daily warning ("exhort one another every day") | Deu 9:4–7; Psa 95:7–11; Heb 3:12–13 | S | 10.0 (already has Deu 9:4), NS-M3 | W; feeds NS-M3 |
| AN-91 | **Meribah's inner seat is named only in the psalm's retelling: a hardened heart.** The same place is read as God's test, and Levi passed it | Psa 95:8; Deu 33:8–9; Psa 81:7–8 | S | 12 | W |

| AN-92 | **No text hardens God's own heart.** Hardness is said of his hand, arm and sword, never his heart. The root that makes Pharaoh's heart heavy makes God glorious | Exo 14:4, 17; Job 9:4; Mic 7:18 | S (searched negative) | 11 §1, 11 §8 | W (11 §1 already says "I have found no text in which God hardens his own heart") |

| AN-93 | **The heavy hand is felt from beneath, and the text corrects the feeling**: "he does not afflict from his heart"; "I knew you to be a hard man", said from fear and condemned; the heaviness ended at confession | Lam 3:7, 31–33; Mat 25:24–26; Psa 32:3–5; Isa 59:1–2; Mal 3:13–16 | S | 11 §8, 10.8 | W |
| AN-94 | **The one refusal in God's own seat**: "my heart would not turn toward this people" (Jer 15:1). It is not hardening | Jer 15:1 | S | 11 §8 | W |

| AN-95 | **The hand does not change; the person's position before it does**: "strong hand" toward Egypt, toward Israel, and then against Israel | Deu 4:34; 6:21; Jer 21:5 | S | 11 §4 | W (change of character: position) |
| AN-96 | Quick temper and evil devices, side by side | Pro 14:17 | 10.3 (woven) | W, done |
| AN-97 | God's intent carried by his anger, understood afterwards | Jer 23:20; 30:24 | 10.3 (woven); NS-M2 | W, done; NS-M2 |
| AN-98 | Nations rage and peoples plot, in one line | Psa 2:1; Act 4:25 | 10.3, 10.4 | W |
| AN-99 | The sufferer feels God's reckoning as enmity ("counts me as his adversary") | Job 19:11; 13:24 | 11 §4 (13:24 woven) | W |
| AN-100 | The mind's desires and "children of wrath" | Eph 2:3 | 13 | W |
| AN-101 | Saul's anger at the song becomes a plan to make David fall | 1Sa 18:8 → 18:25 | 10.0, 10.3 | W |
| AN-102 | Quarrel beside anger in prayer | 1Ti 2:8 | 10.3 (woven) | W, done |
| AN-103 | The nations at ease furthered the disaster | Zec 1:15 | 11 §4 (ease) | W |
| AN-104 | Phinehas's zeal counted as righteousness | Psa 106:30–31 | 10.3 (reckoning), 10.8 | W |

| **The nostrils that hold the breath of life** | Gen 2:7; 7:22; Job 27:3; Isa 2:22; Lam 4:20 ("the breath of our nostrils, the Lord's anointed") | The organ as the place where God's breath was given | Life is breathed in at the very place that will later burn (S/R) |
| **God's nostrils in deliverance** | Exo 15:8; 2Sa 22:9, 16 = Psa 18:8, 15 | "At the blast of your nostrils the waters piled up" | The same organ, in God, is the force that saves (S) |
